summary: Sets out how values for the Point-to-Point Protocol, such as protocol numbers, are assigned by IANA, and what review each kind of assignment needs. The goal is to keep PPP extensions orderly while discouraging frivolous additions.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 3818 changes the assignment policy for selected PPP registries: new values require IETF Consensus rather than first-come, first-served. The review is usually handled through the PPP Extensions working group.

questions: how are ppp protocol numbers assigned
what requires ietf consensus in ppp
what does ietf consensus mean for ppp assignments
subtitle: A review requirement for assigning values in selected PPP registries

tldr.problem: Some PPP name spaces continued to attract proposed extensions, while first-come, first-served assignments did not ensure those proposals were reviewed.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC requires IETF Consensus for new values in the listed PPP address spaces, usually through the PPP Extensions working group.
tldr.outcome: RFC 3818 establishes a Best Current Practice for assigning values in the listed PPP registries.

today: RFC 3818 is a Best Current Practice for assignments in the PPP address spaces it lists.

sections.title: Why Review PPP Assignments
sections.content:
PPP and its extensions use many name spaces where values must be assigned. Historically, IANA made later assignments on a first-come, first-served basis.

The RFC notes that some PPP name spaces continue to attract proposed extensions, including extensions described in Informational RFCs that are not otherwise subject to review. Requiring IETF Consensus for the affected assignments ensures proposals are reviewed.
sections.plainLanguage: PPP uses many registries, and some new extensions need values from them. This policy adds a review step before assigning values in the affected registries.

sections.title: The New Assignment Policy
sections.content:
New values in the address spaces listed by the RFC require IETF Consensus, usually through the Point-to-Point Protocol Extensions working group, known as pppext. The list covers protocol numbers, LCP and IPCP codes, configuration options, authentication algorithms, multilink endpoint discriminator classes, bridging values and other PPP fields.

This changes the earlier first-come, first-served policy for these spaces. The RFC does not change PPP packet behavior; it deals with how assigned values are approved.
sections.plainLanguage: For the registries in the list, a request for a new value must receive IETF Consensus. The policy concerns assignment review, not how PPP sends data.

sections.title: Scope and Security
sections.content:
The rule applies to the PPP address spaces named in the RFC; it does not say that every PPP registry uses this policy. The RFC defines the terminology for policies by reference to BCP 26.

The document states that it deals with process, not protocol, under Security Considerations.
sections.plainLanguage: The policy applies to the registries named in the document. The RFC says it addresses process rather than protocol security.

references.text: Simpson, W., Ed., "The Point-to-Point Protocol (PPP)," STD 51, RFC 1661, July 1994.
